statement: When the outcome is energy-related (body weight, BMI, waist, adiposity or diabetes, read by name or by its values against body-size columns), adjusting for reported total energy is disputed because energy may lie on the causal path (over-adjustment) and adiposity drives under-reporting (collider bias), so both adjusted and unadjusted models should be presented; if the outcome cannot be placed, the dispute is stated as a condition.

user_sees: "`bmi` reads as BMI: energy may be on its causal path and a collider, so adjusting for it is disputed."
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §04 (DISPUTED: 'Conditioning on reported total energy here can be simultaneously over-adjustment (mediator) and collider-stratification bias. Present both adjusted and unadjusted models'); audit IN-20, WP13.

statement: A predictor blank on at least 50% of the rows with the outcome measured, and either yes/no-valued or named like a medication, is most likely a skipped question ('not asked') rather than an unknown value, so median or mode fill is wrong for it (it would put every unknown on medication) and leaving such columns out before complete cases is offered.
regime: Any lens; predictors with blanks among rows with the outcome measured.
decision: Missing-values card: likely-not-asked flags and the leave-out offer.
user_sees: "A yes/no medication question blank on 62% of rows: blank usually means not asked." / "Blank on 55% of rows; nothing says the blanks mean not asked."
claimed_basis: M1_CONTRACT §12.4; DRIVE_RUBRIC §4 (median fill on meds_hbp).
notes: The named test uses the real NHANES fixture, where the medication blanks are a documented skip pattern (known truth for that dataset), and fails if those columns are not flagged; it does not test the 50% threshold or the yes/no heuristic in general. NOT_ASKED_SHARE=0.5 at proposals.py:61; medication word list proposals.py:65-69. The recommended fill for not-asked columns is in methods/missing.py (outside area C). | Inventory source id: F6-032.

statement: In an assay table with features in rows, the row means differ by orders of magnitude while the column means barely differ, so a ratio of sd(log10|row means|) to sd(log10|column means|) of at least 4 (with a row spread of at least 0.4) reads as features in rows, a ratio at most 0.25 reads as one row per sample, and anything between is undetermined; this shape reading (after the names cascade) is never stated at high confidence, so the table is never transposed without the user's answer.
regime: At least 6 numeric columns more than half filled and at least 6 rows; feature-annotation columns (m/z, RT, IDs) excluded from the block.
decision: Leading answer of the orientation question (turn the table or not).
user_sees: "Across 900 rows and 24 numeric columns, the rows differ from each other by orders of magnitude and the columns barely differ at all. In an assay table that is what features in rows looks like ..."
claimed_basis: METABOLOMICS_PACK §01 cascade; audit IN-11; thresholds from turbotab/orientation.py:75-79 (no citation).
notes: Also test_the_reading_is_never_feature_major_on_a_real_fixture (known-truth real fixtures). Names cascade at working.py:383-407. Thresholds 4.0 / 0.25 / 0.4 are uncalibrated constants. | Inventory source id: F6-033.

statement: In an assay table a feature abundant in one sample is abundant in every sample, so samples' ranks across features agree (Spearman ρ near 1); when the block's median ρ with the others is at least 0.6, a column whose ρ is below 0.2 is not a sample but a description of the features (m/z, retention time, an ID), and turning the table is refused until the user says which it is.
regime: Turning a features-in-rows table; at least 3 sample columns and 10 features; no declared feature-table answer.
decision: Refusal of the transpose ('not_a_sample'), with exits.
user_sees: "`obs_mass` does not move with the other samples: its ranks across the features agree with theirs at ρ = 0.05, where a typical sample agrees at 0.93. It reads like a description of the features ..."
claimed_basis: audit MA-04; none stated for 0.6 / 0.2.
notes: The test is a constructed metabolomics fixture with a known m/z column (known truth for one case). Thresholds COHERENT_BLOCK=0.6, NOT_A_SAMPLE=0.2 at working.py:455-456; refusal at working.py:626-642. Also a first column of unique whole numbers not named like an ID is refused as 'reads like the features' identifiers' (working.py:589-607). | Inventory source id: F6-034.

regime: Structure stage; a column whose name reads as a person identifier (SEQN, participant_id, eid, USUBJID).
decision: Grain question skipped; one-row-per-unit grain filled in (reopenable).
user_sees: The grain question is stated rather than asked, with a sentence naming the identifier column.
claimed_basis: M2_CONTRACT §10.
notes: Also working.py:884-910 (stated_grain/effective_grain). Uniqueness of a person ID does not rule out clustering by household, site or PSU; the claim is only about repeated rows per person. | Merged duplicates: CW-035 at turbotab/core/interview.py:364 (_grain_gate); turbotab/core/stages/working.py (_stated_grain_reading). | Inventory source id: F6-035.

statement: When a unit's rows are repeats of one measurement, combining them by their mean is recommended because a single measurement is a noisy estimate whose error attenuates associations toward the null and averaging reduces it; when they are different time points there is no default (first, last or change), because averaging destroys the trajectory and the summary depends on the research question.
regime: Repeated grain with a named unit; repeat kind answered or settled (the structure stage's own reading is medium at most and only proposes).
decision: Aggregation menu's Recommended option (mean for repeats; none for time points).
user_sees: "... averaging them destroys the signal — the change over time IS the signal." / "... noise attenuates associations toward the null. Using the mean ... reduces it"
claimed_basis: turbotab/repeats.py:350-410 (measurement-error arithmetic, 'derived'); a lens pack's prior when supplied (e.g. dietary usual intake).
notes: Primary text at turbotab/repeats.py:350-410 (outside area C); structure_previews.py:556-560 repeats it. effective_repeat_kind (working.py:872-881) only uses a settled reading. Attenuation toward the null holds for classical non-differential error in a single exposure; with error in an outcome or confounders it can bias either way. | Inventory source id: F6-036.

statement: When a unit's rows are combined, a fractional-valued number is an amount combined by the chosen method, a category or code takes its most frequent value under 'mean' (and its first record under 'change'), and a whole-valued number that changes within units — or a decimal-written code such as ICD-9-CM 250.02 — may be a code or a count whatever its number of values, so combining waits for the user's answer for each such column rather than a guess.
regime: Repeated grain; rows combined to one per unit.
decision: Per-column combining rule in the working table; refusal until code-or-count answered.
user_sees: "`coffee_cups` holds whole numbers that change within units, which may be codes for categories (combined by the most frequent value) or counts (combined by the mean). Say which ..."
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14.1/§14.3; the gate case (eating occasions averaged to 22.11); audit MA-14.
notes: Also working.py:1456-1499 (column_kinds), 1502-1567 (code_or_count_facts), 1570-1575 (column_rule), 1683-1725. test_wp1_data_identity::test_4_each_column_is_combined_by_what_it_holds pins behavior on a fixture. | Inventory source id: F6-038.

statement: An outcome that varies within a unit cannot be combined without a stated rule, a non-numeric outcome cannot be combined by its mean, and a two-level outcome cannot be combined by its mean because the mean is a share of records, not one of its levels.
regime: Repeated grain; rows combined; outcome varies within some unit.
decision: Refusal of the combining answer for the outcome.
user_sees: "`event` takes two values, so its mean (a share of records) is not one of its levels; keep the first or the last value instead."
claimed_basis: none stated.
notes: test_wp1_data_identity::test_b21_b22_no_column_is_exempt_and_a_binary_outcome_is_not_averaged pins the behavior. 'Any record' outcome (max) is not offered as an alternative. | Inventory source id: F6-039.

statement: Combining by first record, last record or change needs a time column that places at least half of its values in time (numbers, dates readable in one format, or a declared order of text levels); dates that read both month-first and day-first, mixed formats, or undeclared text labels cannot order a unit's records, and records it cannot place are never the first or the last.
regime: Repeated grain; combining method or outcome rule is first, last or change.
decision: Refusal of the aggregation answer; also refused when the ordering column was only proposed, not confirmed.
user_sees: "`visit` holds text labels (`baseline`, `month_6`, ...) that do not say their order. Declare the order of the levels, or choose another column, before combining by change."
claimed_basis: Audit MA-03 (a change from baseline came out wrong-signed when text dates fell back to file order); BLUEPRINT §14.1.
